notes:
A clean six-bullet page on which every bullet really is an action. Rafaela is not a bystander the sentence happens to name -- bullet 2 tells you to speak to her and bullet 3 sends you back to Evi, so Evi's two conversations are genuinely separated by hers and are NOT one marker. The page gives her no grid of her own, only 'next to him', so she takes Evi's (H-6); that is an inference and the step says so.

Bullet 4 is split in two. The journey out to Konschtat Highlands earns its own rung because the thing waiting at the end of it is a ???, which can never carry a marker -- without the travel step the player would be shown nothing at all for that leg. Bullet 5's Tattered mission orders is a TEMPORARY key item, which the page says outright; it resolves as key item 109 and is the only observable thing in the quest, so it is what holds the ??? rung. The Scale Mail is the header's Reward and so proves the quest is over, not that a step is done.

steps.note: the page places her only 'next to' Evi and gives her no grid of her own, so she is recorded at his (H-6)
back to Evi after Rafaela -- not consecutive with step 1, the page really does put her between them
split out of bullet 4 so the leg out of Bastok has a marker of its own; the ??? at the far end cannot carry one
near a windmill around (G-8) -- the grid comes from bullet 4 and the touch from bullet 5. The page calls the orders a Temporary Key Item.

notes:
Three bullets, one of which is a step and a half. Bullet 1 is NOT an action: 'immediately after the previous quest, the Green Thumb Moogle will tell you' is the Mog Garden chain handing itself over at the end of Full Fields, and accepting a quest is already evidence that its first rung is done. Its content -- log from the Arboreal Grove -- is the instruction bullet 2 then has you carry out, so both bullets are cited on the logging step. Bullet 3 is an outcome: the next quest starts on its own.

Nothing here is observable. The header's reward is 'Miscellaneous Crystals and Logging Materials', which is both a reward and unnamed, so no step carries evidence and the ladder rests on its two markers. The sub-bullet about logging three times in a row is a yield note, not a count of anything the quest requires.

The header's Expansion field reads 'Other', which names no expansion, so expansion is null rather than a guess at Adoulin.

steps.note: the grove is 'nearby' and the page gives no grid. The sub-bullet says you can log and harvest from the spot three times in a row at first; the yield is random and unnamed, so there is nothing to observe.
'report to the Moogle afterwards'. Bullet 3 is the outcome of this conversation, not a further step.

notes:
One bullet, one step, and the interesting decision is the start. The header's Start field is empty -- the quest is handed to you at the end of Crystal Guardian rather than by anyone -- so a literal reading leaves the quest with nowhere to begin and no marker at all. The walkthrough names exactly one entity, the Planar Rift you leave Provenance through, and it resolves, so that is recorded as the start; start.raw keeps the header's emptiness. This is the Carbuncle Debacle move: the marker is placed on what you actually interact with rather than removed.

The step is zoned to Provenance, not Walk of Echoes, because that is where you stand when you click the rift -- one step, one zone. The cutscene fires on the far side and both ends this quest and opens Ad Infinitum, which is an outcome and not a second rung.

steps.note: exit Provenance through the rift back to Walk of Echoes. The step is placed in Provenance because that is where the rift is clicked; the final cutscene plays on arrival.

notes:
There is nothing to do and the page says so. Its single bullet -- 'this quest marks completion of the Voidwatch storyline, but cannot be "completed" and will always remain in the Current Quests menu' -- is a statement ABOUT the quest, not an instruction. A verb-scanner would have manufactured a step out of 'completion'; there is no target, no zone, no action and no observable, so the ladder is deliberately empty rather than padded with a rung that could never be satisfied.

The header's Start is empty too and the walkthrough names no entity anywhere, so unlike Endings and Beginnings there is nothing to recover a giver from -- start.npc is honestly null. That leaves the quest with no markable step and no start, which stage C will quarantine and drop, and that is the right outcome: an uncompletable log entry that sits in Current Quests forever should not be drawing arrows anywhere. Confidence is medium because the page is complete about the quest but empty as a walkthrough, not because the reading is in doubt.

notes: Two bullets, two steps, both on Kohlo-Lakolo, so the runtime draws one marker and reads ahead across them -- which is exactly right here, since the only thing that changes between them is whether you are holding a Rarab Tail. 'Obtain and trade him a Rarab Tail' does not earn an obtain rung of its own: the tail is a common drop with no named source on this page, and inventing one would be guessing. 'Behind warehouse #1' is a position, so it goes in the note and not in the target. The Justice Badge and the Star Onion Brigade Member title are the header's rewards and prove only that the quest is over.

steps.note: behind warehouse #1; the conversation is a cutscene

notes:
Three bullets and all three are steps, which is unusual but real: the middle one is a genuine errand into another zone and not an aside. Bullet 1 reads as description ('Gerbaum asks you to...') but it is the conversation that opens the quest, so it is step 1.

The unmarkable rung between the two Gerbaum rungs is deliberate -- the page really does send you away and back. The page names no monster, only 'the monsters in Zeruhn Mines', so mobs is empty rather than filled with a guess; the step keeps Zeruhn Mines as its zone because that is where the page points you, even though the auction house is an equally valid source and would let you satisfy it from anywhere. That branch is not an items_alt: both routes end in the same three pinches of soot, so there is nothing to express as an alternative HOLDING.

The Zeruhn Soot is step 2's evidence and step 3's requirement, never both as evidence -- repeating it would jump the mark straight past the trip the instant the third pinch landed. Fame reads 'B', which is Bastok.

steps.note: he asks you to thin out the pests in Zeruhn Mines
the page names no monster, so none is recorded. Buying the soot off the auction house satisfies this just as well; the zone is where the page sends you, not a place you must be.
all three at once. The soot is step 2's evidence, so it is not repeated here.

notes:
The page contradicts itself about the Lilac. Bullet 2 has you trade one to Goraow and bullet 4 has you trade one to the Grassy Mound, but a traded item is gone and the header's Item Reqs says only 'Lilac' with no count. Either he hands it back, or two are needed, or one of the two trades is wrong -- nothing on the page settles it. Both trades are kept, each asking for one Lilac, because that is what the page instructs; the quest is demoted to medium for it. A player who follows this ladder and finds himself empty-handed at the mound needs one more Lilac, which is the cheapest possible failure here.

Bullets 3 and 4 stay as two rungs even though they are the same Grassy Mound and therefore one marker; the page distinguishes examining it from trading to it and the split costs nothing. Nothing in this quest is observable -- no key item is granted anywhere and the 800 Cruor is the reward -- so every evidence is null and the ladder is carried entirely by its markers. Goraow is written in the wiki's Abyssea form, 'Goraow (A)', which the normaliser folds to 'goraow'. Fame 'amis' is an Abyssea zone code and not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing.

steps.note: northeast of Conflux #5. The header gives no grid; (G-5) comes from bullet 1.
see the quest note -- the page has you trade a Lilac here AND at the Grassy Mound without ever saying you need two
near Conflux #8, at the other end of the zone from Goraow
the same mound as step 3, so the two rungs share one marker

notes:
Two bullets, both Joachim, and the whole quest is the gap between them: start To Paste a Peiste, A Goldstruck Gigas or Megadrile Menace, then come back once all three are COMPLETE. Note the page's own asymmetry -- 'or' for starting, 'all three' for finishing.

Those three quests are deliberately NOT put into gates.prev. prev is the header's Previous chain and means 'finished before this one may be started', while these three are concurrent errands you are meant to be part-way through when you first speak to Joachim; gating on them would hide the quest from exactly the player who is ready for step 1. They are recorded on the steps instead, and prev keeps the header's Dawn of Death.

No step for 'go do the three quests' either: another quest's state is not in any packet this addon sees, so the rung could never be satisfied and both conversations sit on the same Joachim marker anyway. Fame reads 'Abyssea', which is not one of the nine regions and so gates nothing, but the level is kept.

steps.note: you must already have STARTED one of To Paste a Peiste, A Goldstruck Gigas or Megadrile Menace. The header gives no grid; (H-8) comes from bullet 1.
only after all three of those quests are COMPLETE. Nothing in the packets reports another quest's state, so the wait between these two rungs is invisible.

notes:
The same Mog Garden shape as Green Groves. Bullet 1 is written passively -- 'you will be told to pull up your Coastal Fishing Net' -- because the moogle hands the task over at the end of Pond Probing, but the ACTION in it is yours, so bullet 1 is the net step rather than a talk step. Bullet 2 is the return trip. Bullet 3 is an outcome: the cutscene, the bag of Herb Seeds and the automatic start of Seed Sowing all follow from step 2 and none is a rung.

The Herb Seeds are in the header's Reward, so by rule they prove the quest is over and are not step 2's evidence; the fish and rusty items are random and unnamed. Nothing here is observable and the ladder rests on two markers. The sub-bullet's 'Southeast corner of your island' is a position, so it is a note. Expansion reads 'Other', which names no expansion, so it is null rather than a guess.

steps.note: on the beach at the southeast corner of the island, per the sub-bullet; the page gives no grid
'return to the moogle'. Bullet 3 is what follows from this conversation, not a further step.

notes:
Short and only one thing needs judgement, but it matters. The header's Quest Reqs names A Clock Most Delicate and its Previous is empty, and bullet 1 is precise about which it means: 'once you have STARTED the A Clock Most Delicate quest'. Putting that title into gates.prev would gate this quest on COMPLETING it, and A Clock Most Delicate is the umbrella that Deal with Tenshodo is a leg of, so it finishes afterwards -- the quest would be hidden from every player who could actually do it, permanently. prev is therefore left empty and the requirement is recorded on step 1 as a note. 'Started, not completed' has no slot in this schema.

The Clock tower oil is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that the trade is done, and no step carries evidence. The sub-bullet's drop sources are real named monsters, so they ride on the trade step with role 'drop' the way ingredient sources do elsewhere in this corpus, even though they live in Davoi and Monastic Cavern while the step itself is in Lower Jeuno.

steps.note: requires only that A Clock Most Delicate has been STARTED, which is why it is not in prev -- see the quest note
the sub-bullet's sources: Orcish Troopers in Davoi and Monastic Cavern, the Orcish Overlord in Monastic Cavern. The Clock tower oil is the reward, not evidence.
